narrative: Iran's closure of the Strait of Hormuz dominates the weekend headlines, setting up a sharp geopolitical safe-haven bid for the USD and JPY at the Tokyo open. This escalation, paired with Fed Chair Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole pivot, likely pressures EUR/USD from its Friday close of 1.1587 and would support USD/JPY after it finished Friday at 160.04. The crude supply risk may provide a relative floor for AUD/USD (Friday close: 0.7164), though a broad risk-off shift across the G10 would favor the USD's +145bp OIS carry advantage over the EUR. Markets now look toward Wednesday’s RBNZ decision as the next major policy catalyst.
